t: This is the Rondanini Faun, a marble figure in the British Museum's collection. It is built on an ancient torso, which the Flemish sculptor François Duquesnoy completed between 1625 and 1630. He is known to have made at least the limbs and the head, and he gave the figure its faun tail. Look for the broad, flowing movement, a touch of the Baroque that restorers of the day often added. His work on antiques was acclaimed in Rome as absolutely perfect. The faun takes its name from the Palazzo Rondanini in Rome, where it was once kept.
